elements.element: Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.
elements.evidence: § 19.1 (retained, unedited): "Vendor warrants that Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner by qualified personnel, in accordance with industry standards, this Agreement, and each Order Form."

elements.element: Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.
elements.evidence: § 19.1 warrants Services and Deliverables will "materially conform to their documentation and agreed specifications"; edited § 19.2 covers "each Deliverable and software delivered to Customer will materially conform to its documentation."

elements.element: The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.
elements.evidence: Edited § 19.2 sets the conformance period at "ninety (90) days after delivery", and expressly states Vendor has no correction or refund obligation after that date — short of the 12-month preferred period.

elements.element: The Services warranty lasts 90 days.
elements.evidence: § 19.1's Services warranties carry no expiry, and the § 19.2 cut-off is limited to Deliverables and delivered software; an unlimited Services warranty exceeds 90 days.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: § 19.4: "Vendor shall promptly re-perform, repair, or replace the nonconforming item at no charge."

elements.element: Warranty remedies include a refund.
elements.evidence: § 19.4: "Customer may terminate the affected item and receive a refund of Fees paid for it."

elements.element: Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.
elements.evidence: No compliance-with-laws warranty appears in the rendered § 19.1–19.4 language or the cited paragraphs; § 19.3 was not reproduced, so its content cannot be confirmed.

elements.element: Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code.
elements.evidence: Per the finding's own rationale, § 19.3 limits malicious-code cover to code "intentionally introduced by Vendor", which is narrower than an unqualified no-malicious-code warranty, and the redline does not repair it.

elements.element: Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.
elements.evidence: Operation 1 rewrites § 19.2 to read "For ninety (90) days after delivery, each Deliverable and software delivered to Customer will materially conform to its documentation" — an express software-to-documentation warranty at the 90-day floor (deterministic period check passed).

elements.element: Services are warranted for at least 30 days.
elements.evidence: § 19.1 warrants Services performance and Services conformance with no stated expiry; the § 19.2 time bar reaches only Deliverables and delivered software, so the Services warranty runs longer than 30 days.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: § 19.4 (unchanged, and cross-referring to §§ 19.1 and 19.2): "promptly re-perform, repair, or replace the nonconforming item at no charge."

elements.element: Warranty remedies include a refund.
elements.evidence: § 19.4 second sentence gives Customer termination of the affected item plus "a refund of Fees paid for it" if cure fails within a reasonable period.

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete on the operative text: the single edit lifts § 19.2 from fifteen to ninety (90) days and expressly extends it to "software delivered to Customer", while the pre-existing § 19.4 repair/replace and refund remedies (which cross-refer to § 19.2) are untouched.

Preferred level fails on three elements: the software conformance period is 90 days rather than 12 months, the malicious-code warranty in § 19.3 remains narrowed to code "intentionally introduced by Vendor", and no compliance-with-applicable-laws warranty is visible in the rendered or cited language. To reach preferred the drafter would need to state "for twelve (12) months after delivery" in § 19.2, strike "intentionally introduced by Vendor" from § 19.3, and insert an express Vendor warranty of compliance with applicable laws.

Minimality holds: only the numeral and the software scope words in § 19.2 changed. The added phrase is necessary because "Deliverable" is defined as reports, configurations, specifications and similar work product and excludes Vendor Technology, so without it there would be no express software-to-documentation warranty; no survival tails, expense language, procedures or extra remedies were added, and the Customer-unfavourable but pre-existing sunset sentence was correctly left in place rather than deleted.

Intent is preserved: § 19.4's remedy cascade, the non-exclusivity carve-out for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims, and § 19.1's undated Services warranties all survive without contradiction, and no cross-reference or defined term is left dangling.

Note for the record: hosted software supplied as a Service may not literally be "delivered" to Customer; if the reviewing team wants the SaaS layer squarely inside § 19.2, consider "each Deliverable and any software delivered or made available to Customer". This is a refinement, not a fallback gap, since § 19.1's undated conformance warranty already reaches Services.

elements.evidence: Operation 1 rewrites § 19.2 to read "For ninety (90) days after delivery, each Deliverable and software delivered to Customer will materially conform to its documentation" — an express software-to-documentation warranty at the 90-day floor (deterministic period check passed).

elements.element: Services are warranted for at least 30 days.
elements.evidence: § 19.1 warrants Services performance and Services conformance with no stated expiry; the § 19.2 time bar reaches only Deliverables and delivered software, so the Services warranty runs longer than 30 days.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: § 19.4 (unchanged, and cross-referring to §§ 19.1 and 19.2): "promptly re-perform, repair, or replace the nonconforming item at no charge."

elements.element: Warranty remedies include a refund.
elements.evidence: § 19.4 second sentence gives Customer termination of the affected item plus "a refund of Fees paid for it" if cure fails within a reasonable period.

You are in-house counsel producing a concise Markdown issues memo from verified findings.
Include: Executive summary; a Markdown table of findings with severity, rule, status and section; Walk-away items; Next steps.
Never invent a section reference or legal conclusion. Use only supplied findings.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal team
**From:** Legal (Customer-side review)
**Re:** Playbook review of Vendor's Master Services Agreement — 18 rules assessed

---

## 1. Executive summary

We reviewed the Master Services Agreement against 18 playbook rules. Ten clauses are compliant and require no redline; eight are deviations, of which two are critical (indemnification and limitation of liability) and three more sit in walk-away territory (exclusivity, licence scope and non-compete).

The core problem is a cluster of one-sided commercial restraints and risk allocations: Vendor takes a one-way indemnity from us with no Vendor indemnity anywhere in the Agreement; both Parties are capped at one month of Fees "without exception", which overrides the Excluded Claims regime in §§ 21.2–21.3; we are locked into a three-year, USD 2,000,000-per-year take-or-pay commitment, sole-source exclusivity for the full term, and a 24-month, unlimited-territory post-term non-compete; the Services licence is revocable at Vendor's sole discretion and excludes Affiliates and contractors; and § 11.1 requires immediate cessation of assistance and permanent deletion of Customer Data with no export.

Several of these restraints contradict § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges that we have made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume or no-hire commitment. That internal conflict supports our position and should be used in negotiation.

The news is better elsewhere. Ownership of Deliverables and Customer Data (§§ 13.2, 14.1–14.4), assignment and change of control (§ 24), termination for convenience (§ 9.4), auto-renewal mechanics and the CPI/3% uplift cap (§§ 8.2–8.3), audit rights (§ 22), governing law and venue (§ 28), insurance (§ 18), and the absence of any liquidated damages, MFN or non-solicit burden on us all sit at or above our preferred position.

## 2. Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | § 20.1 (and dangling cross-reference in § 9.3) | One-way Customer indemnity for "every claim relating in any way to Customer's use of the Services"; no Vendor indemnity anywhere. We added a Vendor defence/indemnity (IP infringement, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused data breach, gross negligence/wilful misconduct) with notice, control of defence and cooperation, and narrowed our indemnity to Customer-provided content and our breach of Applicable Law. |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Deviation | §§ 21.1–21.3 ("Fees" defined at § 1.5) | Mutual cap of one month of Fees actually paid, applying "without exception" and so overriding Excluded Claims. Below the 12-month fallback and below the 6-month floor. We set the cap at the greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, restored the Excluded Claims carve-outs, and conformed § 21.3 to reach our payment obligations generally. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Deviation | § 2.2 (conflicts with § 12.3) | Vendor as sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics for the full three-year term, with no category limit, no 12-month cap and no performance-based exit. We made Vendor non-exclusive, which also resolves the conflict with § 12.3. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 13.1 (cf. §§ 13.2–13.3) | Services licence is revocable at Vendor's sole discretion and expressly excludes Affiliates and contractors. We extended it to Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf and limited revocation to uncured material breach, aligning with § 13.3. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Deviation | § 12.4 (conflicts with § 12.3) | 24-month post-term non-compete, undefined scope, unlimited territory, no internal-development or acquisition carve-out. We converted the prohibition into an express permission, leaving the balance of the sentence intact. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Deviation | § 2.1 (conflicts with §§ 7.1, 9.4, 12.3) | Three-year, USD 2,000,000-per-year take-or-pay "without reduction or termination rights". We removed the commitment and confirmed we pay only for Services used or ordered. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Deviation | § 11.1 (conflicts with §§ 11.2–11.3) | Immediate cessation of all assistance and permanent deletion of Customer Data, with no export or migration support. We substituted up to six months of transition assistance at Vendor's then-current rates and anchored the § 11.2 30-day return to expiry or termination. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | § 19.2 (remedies at § 19.4) | Deliverable/software conformance warranty limited to fifteen days, with no correction or refund obligation thereafter — below the 90-day fallback floor. We extended it to ninety days and confirmed it reaches software delivered to us; § 19.4 remedies preserved. |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | §§ 13.2, 14.1–14.4 (with § 1.8, § 15.1) | Preferred position: present assignment of Deliverables to us, Vendor retained rights limited to Vendor Technology, perpetual/irrevocable/royalty-free licence to us and Affiliates, Customer Data processing limited to service delivery, no joint ownership absent a signed instrument. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | §§ 24.1–24.4 (with § 13.3) | Free Customer assignment to Affiliates and successors; Vendor assignment and change-of-control transfer require our consent; no Vendor exit or repricing on our change of control. Competitor bar is framed as consent-based rather than absolute — noted only. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Compliant | § 9.4 (also §§ 7.1, 22.2, 27.3) | No liquidated damages, penalty, termination fee or minimum-fee charge payable by us; convenience termination is fee-limited with refund of prepaid Fees. |
